newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crudes return to weakness on Brent dips.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crudes return to weakness on Brent dips.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices saw grade trade return to recent form late Wednesday when sweet barrels were done at weaker price differentials.
Traders said swooning dated Brent values cheapened the course for the key Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, after earlier indications put the LLS at steady to firmer levels.
Grade price movement came against the backdrop of a stronger outright crude price.
NYMEX offerings gained nearly 50 cents on the day, supported by short covering and weather forecasts calling for colder-than-normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast.
Futures buying left April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing 50 cts higher at $20.55-65 a barrel, with the gap between front month and May in negative territory around 2-5 cents.
Traders said LLS was done last at a 33 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing, after trading earlier at 27 cts under the marker, and compared to talk at WTI/Cushing -25-30 cts on Tuesday.

Dated Brent retreated to trade at an average of April Brent -55 cts, reflecting the supply glut currently dragging cash crudes lower. Traders said the cargoes Glencore trading company had on offer were in the same price range for U.S. Gulf delivery.
"The dated Brent really weakened the LLS," said a trader.
Also working on the LLS was the narrowing of the WTI/Brent spread to around the 95 cts-$1.00 level for April.
Sour prices were steady most of the session. West Texas Sour/Midland was last done at WTI/Cushing -$2.70, with Eugene Island pegged at $2.50 under the mark.
April Postings Plus sold at $1.63, slightly higher than morning trades at $1.60.
